seo.title: Teradata client for {devices}
seo.description: Log on to Teradata Vantage with TD2 or TDNEGO, over a plain session or TLS, browse databases, users, procedures and macros, and create and alter tables.

header.title: Teradata client
header.lead: Query and edit Teradata with no separate client software, and browse its databases, users, procedures and macros.

bands.title: Connect and log on
text: Enter a host, username and password, and choose TD2 or TDNEGO in Logon Mechanism; Database overrides the account default. Vantage servers that accept TD2 connect without a version check.

The default port carries a plain session. Any SSL mode moves the session to the gateway’s WebSocket endpoint on port 443, which cannot be changed. Verify CA needs a CA certificate, and Verify Identity checks the chain and hostname against it or, without one, the system trust store.
Leave Transaction Mode on DEFAULT unless a script needs ANSI or TERA commit rules and case sensitivity. Import from URL… accepts teradata:// URLs, which macOS does not open as links.

bands.title: Query and edit
text: Databases and users both appear as namespaces, and a tab on another database shares the session, running DATABASE before its statements. Stored procedures are listed in the sidebar and macros under Functions, each opening its source in a read-only tab.
Teradata has no LIMIT, so a table’s first page comes back with TOP and later pages with QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER(). EXPLAIN returns Teradata’s plan as raw text.

bands.title: Structure
text: Create tables and change their columns in the <structure>Structure tab</structure>. A table’s DDL view shows its full definition, constraints included.

moveData: <importData>Import</importData> {importFormats} files, and export a table or a result as {exportFormats}. <copy>Copy To</copy> sends tables, their rows or both to another Teradata connection; a copy to a different engine is refused.

faq.question: Why is my logon mechanism ignored?
faq.answer: Type it in uppercase. A value the driver does not recognise, such as a lowercase tdnego, is read as TD2.

faq.question: How do I know the session is encrypted?
faq.answer: Test with Required (skip verify) or a verify mode. Preferred falls back to a plain session when the TLS port is unreachable, so a failed handshake still looks like a successful connect.
